ring_closure_theorem: The W(3,3) observable algebra is a three-layer closed ring. Layer 1 (Mixer) is generated by C=8/13, T=5/13, D=3/13. Layer 2 (Projection) is generated by P(A)=A/Phi3. Layer 3 (RG Closure) is generated by the QCD one-loop beta coefficient b0=7=Phi6, which identifies the beta function with the threshold projection atom, closing the ring: P(Phi6)=b0/Phi3=7/13, P(Phi6)^{-1}=Phi3/b0=13/7. Cross-products of the beta inverse with the mixer tokens produce the Phi6-denominator sector {3/7, 5/7, 8/7, 10/7}, which are the RG-elevated heavy-sector observables.

physical_interpretations.5/7: lepton/quark threshold ratio in Phi6-polar basis
physical_interpretations.8/7: carrier above threshold — heavy KK/GUT partner band

interpretive_note: This is the capstone of the CXLIII-CL construction. The fact that b0=7=Phi6 is not a coincidence: W(3,3) selects Nc=3 quarks and Nf=6 active flavors at the unification threshold, and the one-loop QCD running is governed by precisely the same integer that acts as the Phi6-polar threshold atom. The ring closes because RG running, carrier/threshold mixing, and projective normalization are all aspects of one algebraic object.
